rfi.title: 'An invisible avalanche': what happened in Cameroon's 1986 Lake Nyos disaster?
rfi.description: On 21 August, 1986, 1,746 people died from carbon dioxide poisoning after gas escaped overnight from the bottom of Lake Nyos in Cameroon. RFI examines what happened in the world's deadliest "limnic eruption" and how, 40 years later, our understanding of the danger posed by volcanic lakes is still evolving.

rfi.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak 'growing exponentially' with more than 2,500 dead
rfi.description: The Ebola outbreak raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo is growing "exponentially", with more than 2,500 deaths recorded and half of those in the last 20 days, the senior UN coordinator on the disease said Friday.

rfi.title: France backs down on plan to make patients pay more for healthcare
rfi.description: The French government has scrapped plans to double the annual ceiling on out-of-pocket charges for medicines, medical appointments and other healthcare, after criticism from patient groups and health professionals. The cap was due to rise from €100 to €200, but the government will instead pursue a smaller increase linked to inflation.

rfi.title: France and European allies press Israel to abandon West Bank settlement plan
rfi.description: France has joined Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom in calling on Israel to halt the expansion of settlements illegal under international law in the occupied West Bank, and immediately withdraw tenders issued this week for more than 1,200 new homes under the controversial E1 project.

rfi.title: Cameroon’s President Biya home after 73-day absence, amid health speculation
rfi.description: Cameroon’s President Paul Biya has returned to the country after spending 73 days abroad, ending an unusually long absence that has intensified speculation around the 93-year-old’s health and raised questions over Cameroon's political future.

rfi.title: Millions in France report eco-anxiety after summer of heatwaves and wildfires
rfi.description: Record-breaking heatwaves, drought and wildfires are driving a surge in eco-anxiety across France, with some sufferers "paralysed" by panic attacks, unable to work and, in the most severe cases, experiencing suicidal thoughts.

rfi.title: UN holds second informal straw poll for next leader
rfi.description: The UN's most powerful body, the Security Council, meets Friday to hold another straw poll to gauge the popularity of a growing field of contenders to lead the embattled organisation.

rfi.title: Deadly border mine collapse exposes risks behind Central Africa's gold rush
rfi.description: A deadly landslide at a gold mine on the Cameroon-Central African Republic border has triggered calls for greater oversight of mining operations, after dozens of people were killed and many more were reported missing.

rfi.title: West Bank village siege fuels concern over growing settler violence
rfi.description: Palestinian families remained trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank village of Qusra for an 11th day on Thursday, in a case that has drawn condemnation from US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and become a symbol of growing settler violence in the territory.

rfi.title: Spain to open shelters in Ceuta for migrants and transfer 500 girls to mainland
rfi.description: Spain will open temporary shelters for up to 1,800 migrants in Ceuta, its enclave in Morocco, as authorities tackle the humanitarian crisis resulting from tens of thousands of people attempting to enter the territory last month. The government is also preparing to transfer 500 unaccompanied migrant girls to mainland Spain, despite opposition from Ceuta authorities.

rfi.title: French hospital helicopter landings disrupted by illegal prison delivery drones
rfi.description: Emergency helicopter landings at Strasbourg University Hospitals have been suspended over the risk of collision with drones used to illegally deliver items to inmates in a nearby prison. The hospital says the resulting detour could be "life-threatening" for patients.

rfi.title: Five years on from first vaccine, fight against malaria sees progress in Africa
rfi.description: On World Mosquito Day, attention remains focused on the devastating impact of the disease in Africa. The continent accounts for 95 per cent of malaria-related deaths worldwide. Five years after the roll-out of the first malaria vaccine, it is beginning to deliver measurable results – although significant challenges remain.

rfi.title: Rights group calls for release of two French journalists held in Togo
rfi.description: Two French journalists detained in Togo since late July have been placed in pre-trial detention and charged with "false statements", Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has said, calling for their immediate release.

rfi.title: French winegrowers begin record early harvest as heat and drought bite
rfi.description: Drought and heatwaves have pushed French winegrowers to start picking grapes weeks ahead of schedule, with this year seeing some of the earliest harvests on record – a sign of how climate change is reshaping the wine calendar across the country.

rfi.title: July heatwave sees 1,243 deaths in France, bringing summer toll to 7,300
rfi.description: More than 1,200 excess deaths were recorded in France during the country's July heatwave, bringing the provisional death toll from extreme temperatures this year to 7,300.

rfi.title: Twenty years after Probo Koala, Africa still grapples with ‘waste colonialism’
rfi.description: Twenty years after toxic waste from the cargo ship Probo Koala was dumped across Abidjan in Côte d'Ivoire, the disaster remains an open wound for many victims and a symbol of wealthy countries sending unwanted waste to Africa.

rfi.title: Liberia to take in up to 1,200 US deportees within a year
rfi.description: Liberia has announced it will receive up to 1,200 foreign nationals deported from the United States – one of the largest known deals struck with African countries as part of President Donald Trump's unprecedented bid to drive out undocumented migrants.

rfi.title: Nigeria election campaign begins as voters grapple with inflation crisis
rfi.description: Campaigning kicks off in Nigeria Wednesday, five months ahead of elections set to be dominated by crushing inflation and President Bola Tinubu's economic reforms.

euronews.description: Two personal finance experts urge Portuguese taxpayers to overcome inertia and secure complements to their pensions beyond state social security, after a report on the system's sustainability revealed weaknesses.

euronews.description: Italy has been battered by a severe weather front, with violent storms, gale-force winds and intense lightning, hitting Liguria, Lombardy and northern Tuscany, causing floods and damage.

euronews.title: Syrians who came home after al-Assad's fall find a complicated reality
euronews.description: Nearly 3.6 million Syrians have returned since al-Assad's fall to destroyed homes, dysfunctional bureaucracy, power cuts and wages a fraction of what they earned abroad. euronews.description: Europe is facing a growing mosquito-borne disease threat — and the continent’s ability to fight it remains uneven, according to the EU’s disease prevention agency.

france24fr.description: La Russie a mené des exercices de tirs de missiles au large des îles Kouriles du Sud, revendiquées par le Japon. Ces manœuvres interviennent quelques jours après une visite de Vladimir Poutine sur l'archipel, sur fond de tensions entre Moscou et Tokyo.

france24fr.title: Qui pour succéder à Antonio Guterres au poste de Secrétaire général de l'ONU ?
france24fr.description: Les 15 membres du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU se réunissent vendredi pour un deuxième vote indicatif sur les huit candidats en lice pour succéder à Antonio Guterres. La procédure se déroule dans un contexte de profondes divisions au sein de l'organisation, sous pression notamment des États-Unis de Donald Trump. Tour d'horizon des candidats en lice.

france24fr.title: Martinique : les étudiants en médecine inquiets face à la réduction du nombre de postes d'internes
france24fr.description: Les étudiants en médecine de Martinique sont inquiets après l'annonce d'une diminution du nombre de postes d'internes aux Antilles. Les meilleurs choisiront leur affectation, les autres seront déplacés, notamment vers l'Hexagone. En Martinique, où les besoins de soin sont grands, un étudiant et un député lancent l'alerte.

france24fr.title: Finale du Mondial 2026 : de lourdes sanctions tombent pour les Argentins Paredes et Molina
france24fr.description: Après les incidents qui ont émaillé la finale du Mondial 2026, la Fifa a annoncé suspendre pour dix matches le milieu argentin Leandro Paredes, tandis que son coéquipier Nahuel Molina a écopé d'une suspension pour sept rencontres.

france24fr.title: La forêt de Fontainebleau rouvre au public ce samedi
france24fr.description: Le 12 juillet dernier, un gigantesque incendie avait ravagé près de 10% de la surface de la forêt de Fontainebleu. Elle va rouvrir au public ce samedi 22 août.

france24fr.title: L'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC "progresse de façon exponentielle", alerte l'ONU
france24fr.description: L'épidémie d'Ebola a déjà fait plus de 2500 morts en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) et "progresse de façon exponentielle", a alerté vendredi Julien Harneis, coordinateur principal d'Ebola pour les Nations unies.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : des manifestations face à un été de coupures d'électricité, d'eau, et de pénuries
france24fr.description: En Tunisie un millier de personnes ont protesté dans les rues de la capitale à l'appel de partis politiques et de militants de la société civile après une saison estivale éprouvante. Coupures d'électricité en juillet, coupures d'eau à répétition dans plusieurs régions et pénuries de bouteilles d'eau minérale, le quotidien des Tunisiens devient de plus en plus compliqué.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : la vitesse de propagation d'Ebola inquiète
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, l’épidémie est passée d’une à six provinces en trois mois. Une vitesse de propagation qui inquiète les autorités sanitaires. Parmi les principaux points de vigilance : le fleuve Congo, qui pourrait devenir une nouvelle voie de propagation du virus. Pour y faire face, les autorités congolaises ont présenté le dispositif "Fleuve Congo sans Ebola". Notre correspondante Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula nous en dit plus.

france24fr.title: Ligue 1 : le PSG sans concurrence dans un championnat en crise
france24fr.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain s'avance encore en grand favori pour remporter cette nouvelle saison de Ligue 1 qui reprend vendredi. Quintuple championne de France et double championne d'Europe, l'équipe de Luis Enrique bénéficie également de moyens surdimensionnés dans un  championnat à la peine financièrement.

france24fr.title: Football : Ronaldinho rechausse les crampons à 46 ans
france24fr.description: À 46 ans, Ronaldinho s'apprête à retrouver les terrains plus de dix ans après son dernier match officiel. Le Ballon d'Or 2005 rejoint Ravenne, en troisième division italienne, avec un objectif symbolique : inscrire ce qu'il présente comme son "300e but".

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : Notre-Dame de la Paix, une basilique toujours au frais malgré le climat
france24fr.description: La basilique Notre-Dame de la Paix à Yamoussoukro est considérée comme la plus grande basilique au monde. Malgré un climat tropical, les fidèles y sont toujours au frais.

france24fr.title: Cuba : l'île asphyxiée par Washington manque d'eau
france24fr.description: À Cuba, la pénurie d'eau est de plus en plus préoccupante. Une conséquence directe du blocus américain, car l'approvisionnement en eau est lié au carburant. C'est situation pourrait favoriser les épidémies.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : le projet de colonie israélienne E1 dénoncé par Paris Londres Berlin et Rome
france24fr.description: L'Allemagne, la France, l'Italie et le Royaume-Uni ont appelé jeudi 20 août Israël à "mettre fin à l'expansion des colonies en Cisjordanie" et à "retirer immédiatement" les appels d'offres lancés cette semaine concernant la construction de plus de 1 200 logements pour le vaste projet E1.

france24fr.title: Israël met en garde la Turquie contre toute "aventure dangereuse" en Syrie
france24fr.description:
Le ministre israélien ⁠de la Défense, Israel Katz, a déclaré jeudi 20 août que le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan entraînait la Turquie dans "des aventures dangereuses en Syrie", et qu'Israël ne permettrait à aucune entité de menacer sa propre sécurité.
 
Les relations entre la Turquie et Israël, dégradées en raison d'échanges de plus en plus vifs au sujet de la Syrie - où les armées des deux pays sont actives - se sont davantage détériorées cette semaine, alors que l'Etat hébreu a frappé un

france24fr.title: Football : Ronaldinho revient à 46 ans en 3e division italienne
france24fr.description: L'ancien phénomène du football brésilien Ronaldinho va tenter à 46 ans de marquer "un 300e but", avec Ravenne, ambitieux club de 3e division italienne qui orchestre son inattendu retour sur les terrains, a-t-il expliqué jeudi.

france24fr.title: Colonies en Cisjordanie : quel sera l'impact du positionnement de Paris, Londres, Berlin et Rome ?
france24fr.description:
La France, l'Italie, la Grande-Bretagne et l'Allemagne ont appelé jeudi Israël à "mettre fin à l'expansion des colonies en Cisjordanie" et à "retirer immédiatement" les appels d'offres lancés cette semaine concernant la construction de plus de 1200 logements pour le vaste projet E1.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : nouvelle manifestation contre les coupures d'eau et d'électricité
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, plus d’un millier de personnes ont manifesté à Tunis, la troisième mobilisation depuis juin. À l’appel de partis et de militants de la société civile, ils dénoncent les coupures d’eau et d’électricité à répétition, ainsi que les pénuries d’eau minérale en plein été.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Mehrere Tote und über 50 Verletzte nach Angriff auf ukrainisches Einkaufszentrum
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Dies sind die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Bei einem Schwertangriff an einer Schule in Schweden werden mehrere Personen verletzt
nzz.description: Der mutmassliche Täter ist laut den Behörden festgenommen worden.

nzz.title: Nach einem Ausraster im verlorenen WM-Final wird der Argentinier Leandro Paredes für zehn Spiele gesperrt
nzz.description: Die Tumulte nach dem WM-Final haben Folgen: Drei argentinische Spieler werden gesperrt. Auch ein Spanier wird bestraft.

nzz.title: Ein politisches Bekenntnis im Kampf gegen die Radikalisierung
nzz.description: Gewalttätiger Extremismus unter Jugendlichen ist zu einem Problem für die innere Sicherheit geworden. Bund, Kantone und Gemeinden reagieren nun mit einem Leitfaden.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Konservative Frauen, linke Männer – Meloni und Frederiksen sind die Taktgeber der Migrationspolitik, doch die Linke setzt lieber auf ihre eitlen Katastrophenkapitäne
nzz.description: Das konservativ-sozialdemokratische Power-Duo liefert in der Migrationspolitik, während andere nur versprechen. Von der Linken erhalten die beiden dafür keine Anerkennung, sondern Spott und Vorwürfe. Das hat Tradition.

nzz.title: Schweizer Tourist auf Bali wegen Video auf Social Media zu einem Jahr Haft verurteilt
nzz.description: Ein Schweizer hielt sich während eines religiösen Feiertags nicht an die Regeln und filmte sich dabei. Geltungssüchtige Touristen treffen in Südostasien zunehmend auf eine empörungswillige Bevölkerung.

nzz.title: In der Premier League zeichnet sich eine unberechenbare Saison ab – das liegt am Abgang von Pep Guardiola und vielen anderen Trainerwechseln
nzz.description: In der englischen Fussballliga sortiert sich das Feld gerade neu. Am Freitag startet die neue Saison. Aussichtsreichster Kandidat ist der Titelverteidiger Arsenal.

nzz.title: Arbeitgeber nehmen Mehrwertsteuererhöhung für 13. AHV-Rente in Kauf
nzz.description: Aus Erleichterung darüber, dass eine Mischfinanzierung mit Lohnprozenten verhindert werden konnte, hat der Arbeitgeberverband Stimmfreigabe zu einer AHV-Finanzierung über eine Mehrwertsteuererhöhung beschlossen. Darauf hatten die Gewerkschaften gewettet –, und sie planen schon den nächsten Zug.

nzz.title: Die USA eskortieren Schiffe durch die Strasse von Hormuz: Iran verliert die absolute Kontrolle über die Meerenge
nzz.description: Von der amerikanischen Marine beschützt, transportieren Tanker derzeit täglich mehrere Millionen Fässer Rohöl durch den Wasserweg. Der Geleitschutz ist Teil eines amerikanischen Strategiewechsels im Kampf gegen Iran.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Millionenrechnung nach verlorenem Prozess für Prinz Harry und Elton John
DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Israel blockiert Einsatz einer internationalen Stabilisierungstruppe in Gaza +++ Mindestens zehn Tote nach israelischen Angriffen
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Flüchtlingskrise in Ceuta: Ein Einblick in die angespannte Lage der Gestrandeten
nzz.description: Tausende Migranten harren in der spanischen Exklave in Afrika aus. Die Bewohner sind mit ihrer Kraft am Ende. Besuch in einer Stadt am Rande des Nervenzusammenbruchs.

nzz.title: Polens prominenter Justizflüchtling will in die Heimat zurück
nzz.description: Der frühere Vizejustizminister Romanowski wird von der polnischen Justiz gesucht. Mittlerweile ist er im russisch beeinflussten Transnistrien aufgetaucht. Über die Hintergründe seiner Flucht gibt es wilde Spekulationen.

nzz.title: Die Zürcher Verkehrsbetriebe verschieben den Ausbau von Tramlinien – wegen eines anhaltenden Problems
nzz.description: Das Tramnetz Süd kann zum Fahrplanwechsel nicht vollständig umgesetzt werden: Der 6er fährt vorerst nicht zum Letzigrund. Auch der 10er kann die anderen Linien erst später entlasten.

zeit.title: Kriminalität: Streit eskaliert – Mann mit Messer verletzt
Sparmaßnahmen bei Volkswagen: VW-Chef Blume: «Die Lage ist mehr als kritisch»
Wahlkampfspende an AfD: 10.000 Euro an die AfD. Von einem CDU-Bürgermeister
zeit.description: Mit einer Spende an die AfD plant ein CDU-Politiker in Sachsen-Anhalt die Brandmauer einzureißen. Wie sieht seine Partei das? Und: Ebola im Kongo so tödlich wie noch nie

zeit.title: Volkswagen: Lage bei VW laut Konzernchef Oliver Blume »mehr als kritisch«
zeit.description: Die bisherigen Einsparungen bei VW reichen nach Angaben von Oliver Blume nicht aus. In einem internen Interview bezeichnet er den Konzern als »überdimensioniert«.

zeit.title: Unfälle: Motorradfahrer in Lebensgefahr - Autofahrer flüchtet
Radsport: D-Tour: Nachwuchssprinter stiehlt Franzose Magnier die Show
Klage gegen Daily-Mail-Verlag: Prozess verloren: Millionenrechnung für Prinz Harry und Co.
Verbraucherschutz: Französische Behörden rufen Zehntausende unsichere Kondome zurück
zeit.description: In Frankreich sind Kondome in Umlauf, die nicht den Standards entsprechen. Die Gesundheitsbehörde ruft betroffene Verbraucher auf, sich auf Krankheiten zu testen.

zeit.title: Bremen-Woltmershausen: Mann wird auf offener Straße angeschossen - schwer verletzt
Tiere: Rabiater Esel attackiert Mann und Frau in Wohnmobil
Zwischenfall in Hofgeismar: Auto rast durch Fußgängerzone - Minister spricht von Unfall
Fifa-Sanktionen: Leandro Paredes für Ausraster in WM-Finale zehn Spiele gesperrt
zeit.description: Die Tumulte nach dem WM-Finale haben Folgen: Drei argentinische Spieler werden gesperrt, Anführer Leandro Paredes gleich für zehn Partien.

zeit.title: Tennis: Weltranglistenerster Jannik Sinner sagt für US Open ab
zeit.description: Tennisstar Jannik Sinner muss wegen einer Knieverletzung auf eine Teilnahme bei den US Open verzichten. Er galt als Favorit beim letzten Grand-Slam-Turnier des Jahres.

zeit.title: Hitzeschutz in Deutschland: Grüne legen Entwurf für Klimanotfallplan vor
zeit.description: Die Grünenfraktion wirft der Bundesregierung gravierende Versäumnisse beim Hitzeschutz vor und hat einen eigenen Notfallplan ausgearbeitet. Er liegt der ZEIT vor.

zeit.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: »Firmen werden sich dreimal überlegen, ob sie noch in Sachsen-Anhalt investieren«
zeit.description: Wählen Menschen AfD, weil es ihnen wirtschaftlich schlecht geht? Reint Gropp, der Präsident des Leibniz-Instituts für Wirtschaftsforschung Halle, hat andere Erklärungen.

observador.title: Turquia pede detenção de Netanyahu através da Interpol
observador.description: A Turquia enviou uma notificação à Interpol para a emissão de um alerta vermelho contra o primeiro-ministro israelita. O pedido de detenção deve-se à interceção e detenção de ativistas da flotilha.

observador.title: Rabo de Peixe lamenta comportamento dos populares
observador.description: Junta de Freguesia de Rabo de Peixe lamenta profundamente os comportamentos de alguns habitantes durante uma operação policial. Reforça que não representam a maioria da população.

observador.title: Autarca feliz com aval para fábrica de aviões militares
observador.description: Autarca saúda "olhar diferente do Governo" em relação a Beja. O reconhecimento segue-se após uma carta de intenção entre o Ministério da Defesa e a Embraer, que irá gerar 300 postos de trabalho.

observador.title: Samsung divide 68 mil milhões em dividendos pelos acionistas
observador.description: A gigante sul-coreana espera que este valor ultrapasse o recorde de 2020, que se situa em 12.530 milhões de euros. Prevê também uma recompra de ações, para aumentar o valor para os acionistas.

observador.title: Sindicato da PSP quer reunião urgente com Montenegro
observador.description: O principal sindicato da PSP recusa negociar só com o MAI e aponta o dedo a Montenegro como "responsável máximo" pelo cumprimento do acordo assinado em 2024.

observador.title: PS quer rede de guardas-noturnos em Gaia
observador.description: Proposta chega a votos na reunião de terça-feira. Partido cita "relatos de insegurança" crescentes e defende modelo de baixo custo já ativo no Porto, Lisboa e Cascais.

observador.title: Angola vacina 9,2 milhões de crianças contra a pólio
observador.description: Campanha decorre até domingo, porta a porta e em postos fixos, com 72.305 profissionais e voluntários. Em maio, a segunda ronda já tinha vacinado mais de oito milhões.

observador.title: As notícias das 16h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Incêndio na Alta de Lisboa obrigou a corte no Eixo Norte-Sul
observador.description: O Eixo-Norte Sul esteve cortado junto à saída para Camarate, devido a um incêndio que surgiu entre a zona da Ameixoeira e Telheiras. A circulação foi restabelecida às 15h00.

observador.title: Um dia todos vamos dizer onde estávamos quando Mora saiu
observador.description: Sem espaço no onze e no banco, Rodrigo Mora deixou o FC Porto onde parecia ter destino para ir à procura da sorte. Amorim e Mourinho vão estrear-se, houve medalhas no atletismo e sonhos no ténis.

observador.title: É "importante que o país saia do seu retangulozinho"
observador.description: País deve "deixar de ideologia" e ver o que os outros países estão a fazer no que diz respeito a mecanismos para complementar o sistema de pensões público, defende Álvaro Santos Pereira.

observador.title: 15h. Livre e Bloco de Esquerda querem alterar PSU
observador.description: Os três partidos entregaram pedido de apreciação parlamentar para que o diploma seja discutido na Assembleia da República. Ainda, morreram dois militares do Exército atropelados na A1, na Mealhada.

observador.title: Harry deve pagar 9,5 milhões de libras ao Daily Mail
observador.description: O Supremo Tribunal britânico deu em julho a vitória no caso ao tabloide. Valor total a ser pago pode ascender aos 34,5 milhões de libras alegados pelo jornal como gastos na sua defesa.

observador.title: Como planear as cidades do futuro?
observador.description: Neste episódio, discutimos como as cidades são desenhadas e de que forma a habitação e os desafios climáticos definem o futuro do território.

observador.title: Suécia. Vários feridos em ataque com espada numa escola
observador.description: Polícia sueca recebeu alerta de "violência mortal em curso" na cidade de Fagersta. Um suspeito foi detido e a polícia continua a realizar diligências no local.

observador.title: 14h. Dois militares morrem após atropelamento na A1
observador.description: O Exército português determinou a abertura de um processo de averiguações para apuramento das circunstâncias do acidente. Ainda, deflagrou um incêndio junto ao túnel da Ameixoeira.

observador.title: Ribeira Grande condena ataque à PSP em Rabo de Peixe
observador.description: O autarca considera o episódio "grave e condenável" e admite dia triste. Saudou o profissionalismo dos agentes ao "lidar com o inesperado" e defende atuação firme das autoridades contra o tráfico.

observador.title: Kochorashvili deixa o Sporting e assina com o Sevilha
observador.description: O médio internacional pela Geórgia foi anunciado pelos "leões" em julho de 2025, vindo dos espanhóis do Levante. Regressa a território espanhol, depois de 26 jogos pelos comandados de Rui Borges.

spiegel.title: Schweden: Mehrere Verletzte bei Schwertangriff an schwedischer Schule
spiegel.description: Die Polizei ist in der schwedischen Kommune Fagersta zu einer Schule ausgerückt. Dort hat eine Person offenbar Menschen mit einem Schwert attackiert.

spiegel.title: FPÖ in Österreich: Wie verändern Rechtspopulisten in den Landesregierungen das Land - Podcast
spiegel.description: Die FPÖ regiert in fünf österreichischen Bundesländern. Was verändert sich dort – und was lässt sich daraus für eine mögliche AfD-Regierung in Deutschland lernen?

spiegel.title: Eugen Block streitet in Dänemark um Umgangsrecht mit Enkeln
spiegel.description: Nicht nur in Hamburg, sondern auch in Dänemark treffen sich die Steakhaus-Familie Block und Christina Blocks Ex-Mann vor Gericht. Dort geht es um das Umgangsrecht des Familienpatriarchen mit seinen Enkeln.

spiegel.title: US Open 2026: Jannik Sinner sagt verletzt ab
spiegel.description: Das Knie macht nicht mit: Der Italiener Jannik Sinner verpasst die US Open in New York. Er sei »sehr traurig«, sagte die Nummer eins der Tennisweltrangliste. Dagegen ist sein größter Konkurrent wieder fit für das Turnier.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Annalena Baerbock, Waffenversteck bei Berlin, Jamal Musiala
spiegel.description: Annalena Baerbock wird von den USA und Russland scharf kritisiert. Die Behörden sind besorgt wegen versteckter Waffen in einem Wald bei Berlin. Und der FC Bayern äußert sich zu Musialas Absencen. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Lyon: Katze entwischt - Familie verbringt Urlaub an Raststätte
spiegel.description: Eigentlich wollte die Familie mit ihrer Katze in den Urlaub in die Berge fahren. Dann entwischte das Tier auf einem Rastplatz bei Lyon. Die Urlauber blieben und suchten.

spiegel.title: Borussia Dortmund macht 21,7 Millionen Euro Verlust
spiegel.description: Das bittere Aus in der Königsklasse war für Borussia Dortmund nicht nur sportlich schmerzhaft. Nach einem Gewinn von 6,5 Millionen Euro im Vorjahr verbucht der BVB nun einen hohen Verlust.

spiegel.title: Klage gegen »Daily Mail«: Harry, Elton John und Co. müssen Prozesskosten in Millionenhöhe zahlen
spiegel.description: Am Ende reichten die Beweise nicht: Nach ihrer Niederlage im Bespitzelungsprozess gegen den Verlag der »Daily Mail« werden Harry, Elton John und ihre Mitstreiter kräftig zur Kasse gebeten.

spiegel.title: Gerichtsentscheid: Unfallflucht mit Carsharing-Auto – wann ist der Führerschein weg?
spiegel.description: Wer mit einem Auto einen Unfall baut und einfach abhaut, muss damit rechnen, seinen Führerschein zu verlieren. Ein Carsharing-Nutzer in Berlin konnte sich seinen allerdings zurückholen – vorerst.

spiegel.title: Uno: Annalena Baerbock und der seltsame Schulterschluss von Russland und den USA
spiegel.description: Mit Großmächten legte sich Annalena Baerbock schon als Außenministerin an. Warum haben sich die USA und Russland nun so auf die Präsidentin der Uno-Generalversammlung eingeschossen?

spiegel.title: »Mascha und der Bär« im Kika : Ukraine sanktioniert Kinderserie wegen angeblicher russischer Propaganda
spiegel.description: Großbritannien und Estland wollen ein Streamingverbot, der ukrainische Präsident bezeichnet »Mascha und der Bär« als Gefahr für die nationale Sicherheit. Auch in Deutschland läuft die russische Serie – im Kinderprogramm. Worum es darin geht.

spiegel.title: Uno: Das sind die acht Bewerber für den Posten des Uno-Generalsekretärs
spiegel.description: Uno-Generalsekretär António Guterres scheidet zum Jahreswechsel aus dem Amt, mögliche Nachfolger bringen sich bereits in Stellung. Unter den Bewerbern sind mehrere prominente Namen. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Gräfenhainichen in Sachsen-Anhalt: Frau von durchfahrendem ICE tödlich verletzt
spiegel.description: Am Bahnhof Gräfenhainichen ist eine Frau an einem Bahnsteig von einem durchfahrenden ICE erfasst worden. Sie starb noch am Unfallort.

spiegel.title: Rostock: Angeklagter gesteht Kokain-Schmuggel auf Segeljacht
spiegel.description: Ein 59-Jähriger aus dem Raum Rostock hat gestanden, im Auftrag der Mafia 264 Kilogramm Kokain von Kolumbien nach Europa transportiert zu haben. Der Prozess findet unter erhöhten Sicherheitsvorkehrungen statt.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Bundesanwaltschaft ermittelt gegen Verdächtigen wegen eines geheimen Waffendepots
spiegel.description: Nach dem Fund eines mutmaßlich russischen Waffendepots bei Berlin hat sich Innenminister Dobrindt geäußert: Ein Verdächtiger sitze in Rumänien in Haft. Auch dort wollte er offenbar Anschläge verüben.

spiegel.title: Israel: Ein Aussteiger berichtet über den rechtsextremen Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir
spiegel.description: Itamar Ben-Gvir und Gilad Sade gehörten derselben radikalen Siedlerszene an. Während Ben-Gvir als Minister dazu aufruft, jede Nacht Palästinenser zu töten, hat Sade sich vom Extremismus losgesagt. Und fordert Sanktionen gegen Israels aktuelle Regierung.

spiegel.title: Erfurt: Statue von Bernd das Brot mit Farbe attackiert
spiegel.description: Seine miese Laune dürfte es nicht verbessert haben: Unbekannte haben die Bernd-das-Brot–Statue mit Farbe besprüht. Es ist nicht die erste Attacke, welche die ikonische Figur über sich ergehen lassen musste.

spiegel.title: Nord Stream: Actionfilm über Pipeline-Sprengung – Dreharbeiten in Kroatien
spiegel.description: Die Sprengung der Nord-Stream-Pipelines soll als Actionfilm in die Kinos kommen, mit den Superstars Adrien Brody und Sean Penn. Ausgerechnet am Rand der Dreharbeiten wurde einer der mutmaßlichen Täter festgenommen.

letemps.title: Plaidoyer pour une approche universelle du racisme
letemps.description:
OPINION. Une lutte contre le racisme perçue comme sélective ou instrumentalisée perd sa crédibilité. A l’inverse, un cadre commun affirme que la dignité et l’égalité ne dépendent ni du poids politique d’une communauté, ni de son histoire particulière, ni de la proximité de ses représentants avec les institutions, écrit l’élue Chadlia Keller

Le plan d’action contre le racisme – sur lequel plan

letemps.title: «S’il te plaît, dessine-moi une stratégie industrielle…»

phys-org.title: Shark DNA could hold answers to how we age
phys-org.description: Age isn't just a number for one of the ocean's top apex predators. It's a mystery University of Georgia researchers are solving. A new UGA study has determined how to estimate the age of sharks by analyzing changes to individual animals' DNA. Known as epigenetic clocks, these scientific age estimators focus on chemical alterations known as DNA methylation to measure wear and tear on an animal's cells, providing a noninvasive, fast and accurate assessment of an animal&#03

phys-org.title: More than half of adults in US say they lack basic statistical understanding
phys-org.description: From the daily weather forecast to a baseball player's batting average to an individual's risk of developing lung cancer, understanding statistics can help people in the United States navigate their lives, according to Mark Ramos, assistant research professor of health policy and administration at Penn State. However, more than half of adults in the U.S. reported knowing little or nothing about basic statistical concepts, according to a recent study led by Ramos.

phys-org.title: Study finds women build strong workplace friendships than men
phys-org.description: Women are more likely to form close-knit friendship groups at work, a Durham University Business School study suggests. The findings are published in the journal Social Networks.

phys-org.title: Lab-grown brain models gain a sense of place
phys-org.description: The human brain is often described as one of the most complex structures in biology, and much of its power comes from how it's organized. Its outer layer, the cerebral cortex, is not one uniform sheet. As the brain develops, it divides into distinct areas that each take on different jobs, from movement and vision to memory, language and social understanding.

phys-org.title: After a wildfire, Britain's moors and heaths can be green again within weeks—but the real recovery takes much longer
phys-org.description: Wildfires that have swept across Britain's upland moors and lowland heaths in unprecedented tinder-dry conditions have left behind expanses of smoking, blackened vegetation.

phys-org.title: We're building a New York‑sized city every month. That's worrying for our climate
phys-org.description: We each need a roof over our heads, classrooms to learn in and offices or spaces to work in. To meet this unprecedented demand for new buildings, globally, we're constructing the equivalent of an entire New York City every month.

phys-org.title: Breaking up of swan families in winter disrupts spring migration
phys-org.description: Young Bewick's swans only survive their first spring migration if they stay with their parents long enough. If they lose their parents in winter, they leave later and are unable to keep up with the rest of the population. As a result, there is a greater chance that they will die in their first year of life.

phys-org.title: Antarctic krill fishing is now concentrated in the exact pattern conservation rules were designed to prevent
phys-org.description: The companies fishing for Antarctic krill have harvested so much so quickly that the season had to close in August 2026, three months before it was scheduled to end. That's the second consecutive year of an early closing.

phys-org.title: Quantum dots keep their glow under heat after dual modification
phys-org.description: Quantum dots are semiconductor crystals only a few nanometers in size. Their ability to produce bright, precisely tunable colors has made them promising materials for light-emitting diodes, displays, solar cells and other optoelectronic technologies. Yet heat remains a major obstacle to their practical use.

phys-org.title: 'Rainbow-on-a-chip' could help unlock 6G networks and precision timing for quantum technologies
phys-org.description: Loughborough University physicists and an international team have demonstrated that a grain-of-rice-sized microchip can be used to produce a spectrum of precisely spaced frequencies of light, which is then converted into multiple high-frequency electromagnetic signals known as millimeter waves.

phys-org.title: Women in politics face more personal, sexualized attacks than men, a recent analysis shows
phys-org.description: Online spaces, and social media in particular, are forums for vigorous political debate. They provide a space for members of the public to express political opinions, organize and sometimes even interact directly with politicians. While they clearly have democratizing potential, these platforms have also become fertile ground for hate speech, toxic interactions and online violence.

phys-org.title: New solar system models show Earth is no fluke
phys-org.description: Over the past three decades, computer models of planetary system formation have gone from fairly crude representations to sophisticated simulations using thousands of different starting points.

phys-org.title: Blood-camouflaged nanoparticles defeat drug-resistant breast tumors in mouse model
phys-org.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant subtypes of breast cancer, accounting for 15% to 20% of all cases. Unlike other breast cancers, TNBC lacks targetable receptors, leaving patients dependent largely on chemotherapy, with limited treatment options.

phys-org.title: Q&A: How Brown University is navigating the rise of generative AI use in the classroom
phys-org.description: In just a few short years, generative artificial intelligence tools have made a leap from novelties that produce stilted text to genuine societal disruptors that may alter the way people learn, work and even think.

phys-org.title: What dandelions and bees can teach us about our responsibilities to the natural world
phys-org.description: In spring, on the traditional and treaty lands of the Mississaugas of the Credit, young children, Anishinaabe storytellers and educators walk together with Aki (Land) and Nibi (Water).

phys-org.title: Interplanetary spacecraft capture a coronal mass ejection component hidden from Earth
phys-org.description: During a coronal mass ejection (CME), the sun hurls billions of tons of magnetized plasma into space. These eruptions are among the most powerful events in the solar system, and when they are aimed toward Earth, they can seriously threaten the satellites and power grids we depend on. For now, it remains notoriously difficult to predict how these eruptions evolve over time—and, in turn, whether they might be heading toward us.

phys-org.title: Forest service detects emerald ash borer in 5 additional counties
phys-org.description: The Texas A&M Forest Service has confirmed emerald ash borer in Delta, Erath, Hardin, Walker and Wood counties, continuing the spread of the invasive insect into new areas of Texas. Eight new counties have been confirmed with detections this year.

phys-org.title: Leaving abusive relationships can be harder for migrant women. Here's what they need to feel safe
phys-org.description: Like many women raised in traditional cultures and religious contexts, I was taught that a "good" woman holds the family together. In my culture, women were often glorified for quietly accepting hardship.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

proj-syn.title: MDBs Are Becoming a New Global Safe Asset
proj-syn.description: Even as multilateralism faces an existential threat, multilateral development banks are not only surviving but thriving. Thanks to MDBs’ ability to borrow at costs close to that of the US Treasury, they have created a new class of de facto risk-free assets that could help underpin the global financial system.

proj-syn.title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
proj-syn.description: What is the apparent fragility in the US bond market telling us? Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

proj-syn.title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
proj-syn.description: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention. Yet the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Three Ways AI Will Change the Course of Humanity
proj-syn.description: The AI debate has largely focused on productivity gains and job displacement, but its consequences will reach much further By revolutionizing how we combat disease, wage wars, and stimulate income growth, AI could fundamentally alter the terms of human existence.

proj-syn.title: Global Economic Convergence Is Stalling
proj-syn.description: For a while, the world’s advanced economies (other than the US) were rapidly losing ground to their emerging counterparts. But the BRICS' catch-up momentum has stalled since 2016, not because the G7 has been doing better, but because everyone has been doing worse.

proj-syn.title: When a Big Energy Project Turns Bad
proj-syn.description: After hundreds of millions of dollars were invested by developing-country governments, and before a single watt of energy was transferred, the CASA-1000 infrastructure project in Central Asia has effectively failed. The international institutions that conceived, financed, and promoted the project must answer for this.

proj-syn.title: The Trolling of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: Democracy is most vulnerable when voters can no longer distinguish genuine abuses of power from partisan attacks. Authoritarian leaders exploit that uncertainty by blurring the line between misconduct and political theater, making legitimate criticism look like just another witch hunt.

proj-syn.title: A Future With Chinese Characteristics
proj-syn.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American, and even American young people.

proj-syn.title: Putin Has Run Out of Moves
proj-syn.description: Even with the Russian economy suffering from low growth, high inflation, and relentless Ukrainian long-range drone strikes on energy infrastructure, President Vladimir Putin has thrown fiscal caution to the wind and allowed the government’s budget deficit to balloon to 2.8% of GDP. It isn’t likely to end well.

proj-syn.title: The Geopolitical Drag on AI Governance
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration’s decision to prioritize national competitiveness over multilateral frameworks has deepened the fragmentation of AI governance—and expanded the opening for China to organize its own system. But China's approach is similarly shaped primarily by its own geopolitical ambitions.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of the China Shock
proj-syn.description: As advances in generative AI continue, US policymakers should heed two lessons from the opening of trade with China. But that will require them to rethink the conventional wisdom about deindustrialization and the decline of manufacturing employment.
